explanation: 11-speed chains are effectively interchangeable across brands: Shimano, SRAM and KMC 11s chains all run quietly on each other's 11-speed MTB cassettes.
10-speed chains are interchangeable across brands on 10-speed cassettes.
A Shimano Hyperglide+ 12s chain runs fine on a SRAM Eagle cassette — widths are close enough (5.25mm inner).
caveats: You lose the Hyperglide+ directional shift-ramp benefit, which only works on Shimano 12s cassettes.
Mind the chain's direction marking when installing — HG+ chains are directional.

explanation: A SRAM Eagle chain works on a Shimano 12s Micro Spline cassette; shifting is good, though Shimano recommends a Hyperglide+ chain for best performance.
caveats: Slightly less crisp shifting than a Hyperglide+ chain on Shimano ramps.

explanation: KMC X12 is designed and marketed as compatible with both SRAM Eagle and Shimano 12-speed drivetrains.

Shimano 11s MTB shifters pull about 1.1mm of cable per shift (Dyna-Sys), while SRAM X-Actuation derailleurs expect a different ratio — the derailleur will move the wrong amount per click and never index across the cassette. This is the classic cross-brand pairing that does NOT work, even though both are '11-speed'.
SRAM X-Actuation shifters and Shimano Dyna-Sys derailleurs use different cable-pull ratios — indexing will be off across the range. Keep shifter and rear derailleur in the same actuation family.
